claims.text: High-entropy alloys span a broad range of compositions.
Expandable-feature machine learning can efficiently predict structural phases in multi-element high-entropy alloys.
High-throughput density-functional theory can screen large HEA composition spaces and predict candidate crystal structures or phase stability.
Combining expandable-feature machine learning with high-throughput density-functional theory can predict HEA melting temperatures more accurately and efficiently than current methods.
The combined approach can improve predictions of melting properties beyond melting temperature.
Crystal structure and phase diagrams mediate prediction of HEA melting behavior.
HEA formation reflects an interplay among mixing enthalpy, intermetallic formation, and melting point.
Machine learning can learn relationships among composition, crystal structure, and melting properties.
The proposed approach will improve both accuracy and computational efficiency relative to traditional prediction methods.
The approach should remain valid across various HEA compositions and processing conditions.
The approach is limited to HEAs with certain compositions and processing conditions.
Performance depends on the quality of the training data.
Performance depends on the complexity of relationships among composition, crystal structure, and melting properties.
A falsification benchmark can compare predicted melting temperature, latent heat of fusion, and solid-liquid interface energy against experimental measurements for a set of HEAs.
Significant deviation of predictions from experimental results would falsify the hypothesis.
